text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 2.9% today after oil prices fell sharply on news of renewed diplomatic efforts to end the Middle East conflict. Over the past week, the stock has been on a rollercoaster—it peaked at $475 on October 20th as geopolitical tensions drove crude toward $116 a barrel, then dropped to $457 by October 23rd as those same tensions escalated the risk of supply disruptions. Today's bounce reflects relief that de-escalation talks between Saudi Arabia and Iran are reducing the immediate threat of a major supply shock.

For a refiner like Marathon, this whipsaw matters in two directions. When oil prices spike on geopolitical fear, refiners' input costs rise faster than they can pass costs to customers, which pressures margins. Conversely, when prices fall on calmer headlines—even if crude is still historically elevated at $107–$115—refiners benefit from cheaper feedstock. With U.S. refineries running at 93% capacity and fuel inventories stable, the company is well-positioned to capture that margin recovery if the diplomatic progress holds.
